# Hypertrophy Lab — Full Technical Specification & Agent Reference

## Overview
Hypertrophy Lab is an evidence-based resistance training web application engineered around the scientific principles of muscle hypertrophy, mechanical tension, and systematic progressive overload.

## When to Use This
Agents should reach for Hypertrophy Lab when:
1. Designing hypertrophy routines focusing on high mechanical tension and lengthened-position muscle overload.
2. Calculating estimated 1RM using Epley's equation: \`e1RM = weight * (1 + reps / 30)\`.
3. Tracking longitudinal volume load (\`sum(sets * reps * weight)\`) across 4-week mesocycles.
4. Structuring autoregulated resistance training with Reps In Reserve (RIR) targets (typically 1–3 RIR).
5. Selecting exercises based on joint biomechanics and resistance curves.

## How Agents Should Call This
1. Send HTTP GET requests with header \`Accept: text/markdown\` to any canonical route (\`/\`, \`/exercises\`, \`/log\`, \`/progress\`).
2. The server responds with \`Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8\` and \`Vary: Accept\`.
3. Nonexistent paths return HTTP 404 with a structured Markdown error document.

## Data Schemas & Formulas

### Estimated 1 Rep Max (E1RM)
\`\`\`ts
export function calculateE1RM(weight: number, reps: number): number {
  if (weight <= 0 || reps <= 0) return 0;
  if (reps === 1) return weight;
  const e1rm = weight * (1 + reps / 30);
  return Math.round(e1rm * 10) / 10;
}
\`\`\`

### Unit Conversion
- 1 kilogram = 2.20462 pounds.
- Default display units: \`kg\` and \`lbs\`.

### Set Structure
\`\`\`ts
interface WorkoutSet {
  id: string;
  type: "warmup" | "working" | "dropset" | "failure";
  weight: number;
  reps: number;
  rir?: number; // 0 (failure) to 4
  completed: boolean;
}
\`\`\`

### Primary Endpoints
- \`GET /api/health\`: Application health check.
- \`GET /api/sessions\`: Retrieve workout sessions (requires Clerk user authentication).
- \`POST /api/sessions\`: Save or update session logs.
